x: The Convention of Wadgaon followed the British defeat at Talegaon in 1779, after which the British had to give up their gains.

s: Which of the following statements regarding the Treaty of Purandar is correct?
o: It abolished the office of the Peshwa.
It was concluded by the Calcutta Council with the Barabhai Council and set aside the Treaty of Surat.
It was concluded between the British and Holkar in 1805.
It gave the British control over the Mughal emperor.
x: The Treaty of Purandar of 1776 was concluded by the Calcutta Council with the Barabhai Council and set aside the Treaty of Surat.

s: Which of the following was NOT a term associated with the Treaty of Bassein?
o: The Peshwa ceded lands yielding Rs 26 lakh.
The Peshwa surrendered Surat to the British.
The Peshwa obtained additional chauth claims on the Nizam.
A subsidiary force was to be maintained in Maratha territory.
x: Under the Treaty of Bassein, the Peshwa gave up his chauth claims on the Nizam; he did not obtain additional claims. The other three were terms of the treaty.

s: Which of the following best describes the result of the Treaty of Salbai?
o: The status quo was restored, the British retained Salsette and peace followed for twenty years
The British surrendered Salsette and recognised Raghunath Rao
The Marathas accepted the Subsidiary Alliance
The Peshwaship was abolished and Poona was annexed
x: The Treaty of Salbai restored the status quo, allowed the British to retain Salsette and ushered in approximately twenty years of peace.

s: With whom did the British sign the Treaty of Deogaon (1803)?
x: Deogaon was with the Bhonsle of Nagpur; Bassein with the Peshwa, Surji-Arjangaon with Scindia and Rajpurghat with Holkar.

s: Between whom was the Treaty of Salbai (1782) concluded?
x: Salbai was signed by the British (Warren Hastings) and the Marathas (Mahadji Scindia), and it ended the First Anglo-Maratha War (APPSC 2018). The British made peace with Mysore at Mangalore in 1784. The Marathas fought the Nizam at Kharda in 1795. The Nizam's treaties with the British came at Masulipatnam (1768) and Hyderabad (1798).

s: In which year did Baji Rao II, whose adopted son Nana Sahib was denied the Peshwa pension, die?
x: Baji Rao II died in 1851, after which Nana Sahib's pension was stopped.

s: Who commanded the British forces at Assaye?
x: Arthur Wellesley commanded at Assaye; Lord Lake at Delhi and Laswari; Gough at Mudki and Chillianwala.

s: With whom was the Treaty of Surji-Arjangaon (1803) signed?
x: Surji-Arjangaon (1803) was with Scindia; the British gained Delhi and control of the Mughal emperor.

s: With whom was the Treaty of Rajpurghat (1805) concluded?
x: Rajpurghat (1805) was signed with Holkar.

s: Which of the following treaties is INCORRECTLY matched with the Maratha party?
x: Rajpurghat (1805) was signed with Holkar, not Scindia.

s: Who won the battles of Delhi and Laswari in the Second Anglo-Maratha War?
x: Lord Lake won Delhi and Laswari; Arthur Wellesley won Assaye and Argaon.

s: With whom did the Bombay government sign the Treaty of Surat (1775)?
x: The Treaty of Surat (1775) was between the Bombay government and Raghunath Rao; Purandar (1776) cancelled it.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Third Anglo-Maratha War:
1. The Peshwaship was abolished in 1818.
2. Baji Rao II was pensioned off.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: After the Third Anglo-Maratha War (1817-18) the Peshwaship was abolished in 1818 and Baji Rao II was pensioned.

s:
Arrange the following treaties in chronological order:
A. Treaty of Bassein
B. Treaty of Amritsar
C. Treaty of Sugauli
D. Treaty of Yandabo
x: Bassein was 1802, Amritsar 1809, Sugauli 1815 and Yandabo 1826, giving A, B, C, D.

s: In which year was the Treaty of Salbai signed?
x: The Treaty of Salbai was signed in 1782. The Treaty of Madras was 1769, the Treaty of Mangalore 1784 and the Treaty of Bassein 1802.

s: Which of the following Subsidiary Alliance states accepted it first?
x: The order was Hyderabad (1798) → Mysore → Oudh → Scindia.

s: Which war was ended by the Treaty of Yandabo?
x: Yandabo (1826) ended the First Anglo-Burmese War; Sugauli (1815) ended the Anglo-Nepal War.

s: Under which Governor-General was the First Anglo-Afghan War fought?
x: The First Anglo-Afghan War (1838/39–42) was under Lord Auckland.

s: Which British general forced Nepal to accept terms in the Anglo-Nepal War in 1815?
x: In 1815, after Almora was won, Ochterlony forced Nepal to accept terms, leading to the Treaty of Sugauli.

s: Which territories did the British gain by the Treaty of Yandabo (1826)?
o: Kumaon, Garhwal and parts of the Terai
x: The Treaty of Yandabo ended the First Anglo-Burmese War and gave Assam, Manipur, Arakan and Tenasserim.

s: With which Governor-General is the Tripartite Treaty of 1838 associated?
x: The Tripartite Treaty (1838) preceded the First Anglo-Afghan War under Auckland.

s: How was the annexation of Sindh described?
x: The British annexation of Sindh was called the ‘Tail of the Afghan Storm’.

s: Which of the following was NOT an objective of the British conquest of Sindh?
o: Recovering prestige lost in the First Afghan War
Securing the trade of the Indus
Introducing the Doctrine of Lapse in Sindh
x: The stated objectives were recovery of prestige after the First Afghan War, countering Russia and securing Indus trade. The Doctrine of Lapse was not an objective of the conquest of Sindh.

s: At which battle did Sir Charles Napier defeat the Amirs of Sindh?
x: Napier defeated the Amirs of Sindh at Miani (and Dabo), and Sindh was annexed in 1843.

s: Besides Miani, at which battle were the Amirs of Sindh defeated by Charles Napier in 1843?
x: Napier defeated the Amirs of Sindh at Miani and Dabo in 1843.

s: Under which Governor-General was Sindh annexed by conquest in 1843?
x: Sindh was conquered in 1843 under Ellenborough (1842-44), before Dalhousie's time.

s: What did Indian states generally retain under British paramountcy?
o: the right to make war on neighbours
x: Indian states kept their internal administration but had no independent international life.

s: Who converted the policy of subsidiary alliances into a wider system of paramountcy?
x: Lord Hastings developed subsidiary alliances into the system of British paramountcy and imposed humiliating treaties on the Peshwa and Scindia.

s:
Consider the following statements about the subordinate alliances of 1818:
1. States such as Udaipur, Jaipur and Jodhpur accepted them.
2. The states gave up control over their external relations.
3. The states lost control of their internal administration.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Rajputana states gave up external relations for British protection but kept internal administration.

s: Under the subordinate alliances accepted by Rajputana states in 1818, the states:
o: surrendered their internal administration but retained foreign relations
were exempted from all British political control
gave up their external relations in return for British protection
became directly administered provinces of the Company
x: The Rajputana states accepted British protection and surrendered control over their external relations under subordinate alliances in 1818.

s: Which Sikh ruler was deposed when Punjab was annexed in 1849?
x: Punjab was annexed by conquest after the Second Anglo-Sikh War (1849) and Duleep Singh was deposed.

s: The Treaty of Amritsar (1809) between Ranjit Singh and the British fixed which river as the boundary?
x: The 1809 Treaty of Amritsar, under Minto I, fixed the Sutlej as the boundary.

s: Which European officers trained Ranjit Singh's Khalsa army?
x: Ventura and Allard (joined 1822) trained the infantry and cavalry of the Khalsa army.

s: In which year did Maharaja Ranjit Singh die?
x: Ranjit Singh died in 1839, not 1836, after which chaos followed.

s: Who was the last Sikh ruler of Punjab?
x: Duleep Singh (1843), with his mother Jind Kaur as regent, was the last Sikh ruler.

s: What was the model brigade of Ranjit Singh's Khalsa army called?
x: Ranjit Singh's model brigade, trained by Ventura and Allard, was the Fauj-i-Khas.

s: Who was the Governor-General of India during the First Anglo-Sikh War (1845–46)?
x: Lord Hardinge was the Governor-General during the First Anglo-Sikh War, fought in 1845–46.

s: Which one of the following was the immediate cause of the First Anglo-Sikh War?
o: The murder of Vans Agnew and Anderson at Multan
The refusal of the Nizam to assign Berar
The Sikh army crossing the Sutlej
The detention of two British doctors in Sikkim
x: The First Anglo-Sikh War began when the Sikh army crossed the Sutlej, whose boundary had been fixed by the Treaty of Amritsar of 1809.

s: What triggered the Second Anglo-Sikh War (1848-49)?
o: the Sikh army crossing the Sutlej
the murder of British officers Vans Agnew and Anderson at Multan
the death of Maharaja Ranjit Singh
the sale of Kashmir to Gulab Singh
x: It began after the British officers Vans Agnew and Anderson were murdered at Multan, under Dalhousie. The Sutlej crossing caused the First war (1845). Ranjit Singh's death in 1839 was the background to both wars. Kashmir went to Gulab Singh in 1846, after the First war.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Gujrat and Chillianwala belonged to the Second Anglo-Sikh War; Mudki and Sobraon to the First.

s: Who led the Sikhs at the Battle of Chillianwala?
x: Sher Singh Attariwala led the Sikhs and Lord Gough the British; the battle was undecided.

s: Under which treaty was Kashmir transferred to Gulab Singh after the First Anglo-Sikh War?
x: Kashmir went to Gulab Singh under a separate Treaty of Amritsar; Bhairowal also followed the First Anglo-Sikh War.

s:
Assertion (A): The Battle of Chillianwala took place on 13 January 1849.
Reason (R): The British fought against the Sikhs in the Battle of Chillianwala.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Chillianwala was fought on 13 January 1849 between the British and the Sikhs. The opponents do not explain the date.

s: The Treaty of Lahore (1846) followed which war?
x: The Treaty of Lahore (1846) followed the First Anglo-Sikh War and extended British control in Punjab.

s: Which treaty of December 1846 made the British Resident the virtual ruler of Punjab?
x: The Treaty of Bhairowal (Dec 1846) made the British Resident the virtual ruler of Punjab.

s: Through whose betrayal did the Sikhs lose the Battle of Sobraon (1846)?
x: Sobraon was lost through the betrayal of Lal Singh and Tej Singh.

s: Which battle decided the Second Anglo-Sikh War?
x: Chillianwala was undecided; Gujrat (21 Feb 1849) decided the war.

s: For what sum was Kashmir sold to Gulab Singh under the Treaty of Amritsar (1846)?
x: Kashmir was sold to Gulab Singh for Rs 75 lakh.

s: Who commanded the British at the Battle of Chillianwala (1849)?
x: At Chillianwala (13 January 1849) Lord Gough fought Sher Singh Attariwala; the battle was undecided.

s: Who annexed Coorg in 1834 on the plea of misgovernance?
x: Bentinck took Coorg in 1834 citing misgovernance, along with Central Cachar.

s: Who was the last Governor-General of Bengal?
x: William Bentinck was the last Governor-General of Bengal and became the first Governor-General of India under the Charter Act of 1833.

s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding William Bentinck’s tenure?
o: He served from 1823 to 1828 and was followed by Amherst.
He served from 1835 to 1836 and was followed by Auckland.
He served as Governor-General from 1828 to 1835 and became Governor-General of India from 1833.
He served as Governor-General only from 1833 to 1835.
x: Bentinck served from 1828 to 1835; after the Charter Act of 1833, he held the title Governor-General of India from 1833 onward.

s: With whom did William Bentinck conclude a treaty of perpetual friendship in 1831?
x: Bentinck concluded a treaty of perpetual friendship with Ranjit Singh in 1831.

s: In which year did Bentinck abolish Sati?
x: Sati was abolished under Bentinck in 1829 (after Wellesley's infanticide measure of 1802 and before Ellenborough's 1843 slavery abolition).

s: Which Governor-General is credited with easing the entry of British investors and traders into India?
x: The APPSC-GS 2025 key names William Bentinck. Warren Hastings is known for abolishing the Dual Government and for the Ring Fence policy. Wellesley is known for the Subsidiary Alliance. Ellenborough annexed Sindh and passed the Anti-Slavery Act.

s: Under which Governor-General was Captain W.H. Sleeman appointed in 1835 to suppress the Thugs?
x: Sleeman was appointed against the Thugs in 1835 under William Bentinck.

s: During whose tenure were the first universities in India established in 1857?
x: The first universities came in 1857 under Canning, not Bentinck.

s: Which goddess did the Thugs worship?
x: The Thugs, both Hindu and Muslim, worshipped Kali (also Durga and Bhavani).

s: Which one of the following pairs of popular titles is correctly matched?
o: Founder of British power in India - William Bentinck
Father of Modern Western Education in India - William Bentinck
x: Bentinck is called the Father of Modern Western Education in India. Robert Clive, not Bentinck, is the founder of British power in India and was also called the 'heaven-born general'. Wellesley called himself the 'Bengal Tiger'.

s: Who is called the 'Father of Modern Western Education in India'?
x: William Bentinck is called the Father of Modern Western Education in India.

s: With whom is the 'Ring Fence' policy associated?
x: Ring Fence was Warren Hastings' policy; non-intervention was Sir John Shore's.

s: Which one of the following measures is associated with Warren Hastings?
x: Warren Hastings abolished the Dual Government in 1772. The Permanent Settlement was introduced by Cornwallis, the Subsidiary Alliance by Wellesley and Sindh was annexed during Ellenborough’s tenure.

s: During whose tenure was the Code of Gentoo Laws (1776) prepared?
x: The Code of Gentoo Laws, Halhed's translation of the Vivadarnavasetu, came in 1776 under Warren Hastings.

s: Who translated the Vivadarnavasetu into English as the Code of Gentoo Laws (1776)?
x: The Code of Gentoo Laws (1776) under Warren Hastings was Halhed's translation of the Vivadarnavasetu.

s: What was the amount of the annual tribute to Shah Alam that Warren Hastings stopped?
x: Warren Hastings stopped the Rs 26 lakh tribute to Shah Alam.

s: During whose tenure as Governor-General was the Asiatic Society of Bengal founded?
x: The Asiatic Society of Bengal was founded (1784) during the time of Warren Hastings.

s: Which Governor-General set up the Diwani and Fauzdari Adalats?
x: Warren Hastings set up the Diwani (civil) and Fauzdari (criminal) Adalats.

s: During whose tenure did the Treaty of Salbai (1782) end the First Anglo-Maratha War?
x: The First Anglo-Maratha War ended with the Treaty of Salbai (1782) under Warren Hastings.

s: Which of the following was among the impeachment charges against Warren Hastings?
o: Application of the Doctrine of Lapse
Introduction of the Subsidiary Alliance with the Nizam
Plunder of the Begums of Awadh
x: The charges included the Rohilla War, Chait Singh, the plunder of the Begums of Awadh and the judicial murder of Nand Kumar.

s: What was the outcome of the impeachment trial of Warren Hastings (1788-1795)?
x: Burke and the Whigs impeached Hastings in 1787; the trial ran 1788-1795 and ended in acquittal.

s: In which year was Warren Hastings impeached in the British Parliament?
x: Hastings was impeached in 1787; the trial ran from 1788 to 1795.

s:
Consider the following statements about the impeachment of Warren Hastings:
1. It was led by Edmund Burke.
2. The judicial murder of Nand Kumar was one of the charges.
3. The trial ended in his conviction in 1795.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Burke and the Whigs led the impeachment and Nand Kumar's judicial murder was a charge; the trial ended in acquittal in 1795.

s: Which ruler of Benares figured in the impeachment charges against Warren Hastings?
x: The charges against Warren Hastings included his treatment of Chait Singh of Benares, the Rohilla War, the Begums of Awadh and Nand Kumar.

s: With whom are the Regulating Act and the Ring Fence policy associated?
x: Warren Hastings is linked with the Regulating Act and Ring Fence policy; Clive with Plassey, Cornwallis with the Permanent Settlement, Wellesley with the Subsidiary Alliance.

s: Which Governor-General died at Ghazipur during his second term in office?
x: Cornwallis returned for a second term in 1805 and died at Ghazipur during that term.

s: Who created the post of District Judge?
x: Cornwallis created the post of District Judge; his Code of 1793 separated revenue from justice.

s: What did the Cornwallis Code of 1793 separate?
o: The Board of Control from the Court of Directors
Revenue administration from the administration of justice
The Company's trade from its political affairs
The Bengal army from the Madras army
x: The Cornwallis Code (1793) separated revenue administration from justice and created the post of District Judge.

s: Who is known as the 'Father of Civil Services in India'?
x: Cornwallis reformed the services and created the Covenanted Civil Service; Warren Hastings only laid the foundation.

s: Who was the Governor-General during the Second Anglo-Mysore War (1780-84)?
x: Warren Hastings was Governor-General during the Second war; Cornwallis fought the Third.

s: Between whom was the Battle of Kharda (1795) fought?
x: At Kharda the Marathas defeated the Nizam while Sir John Shore kept neutral.

s: Who among the following was associated with the Rohilla War of 1774, the First Anglo-Maratha War and the Second Anglo-Mysore War?
x: Warren Hastings was Governor of Bengal from 1772 and Governor-General from 1774 to 1785. His time included the Rohilla War (1774), the First Anglo-Maratha War and the Second Anglo-Mysore War.

s: During which period did Warren Hastings serve as Governor-General of Bengal?
x: Warren Hastings, the first Governor-General of Bengal, held the post from 1774 to 1785.

s: With whom is the policy of non-intervention associated?
x: Sir John Shore followed non-intervention; Hastings the Ring Fence, Cornwallis the Permanent Settlement, Wellesley the Subsidiary Alliance.

s: Who was the Governor-General when the Marathas defeated the Nizam at the Battle of Kharda in 1795?
x: Sir John Shore, Governor-General from 1793 to 1798, followed a policy of neutrality at Kharda, where the Marathas defeated the Nizam.

s: Under which Governor-General did the First Anglo-Burmese War take place?
x: The First Anglo-Burmese War came under Amherst; Auckland had the First Afghan War and Ellenborough annexed Sindh.

s: During which period did Lord Wellesley, who introduced the Subsidiary Alliance, serve as Governor-General?
x: Wellesley ruled from 1798 to 1805, introduced the Subsidiary Alliance and fought the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War.

s: Which treaty is correctly matched with the Governor-General of its time?
x: Amritsar (1809) was concluded under Minto I; Salbai belongs to Warren Hastings and Lahore to Hardinge I.

s: Which of the following pairs of Governor-General and treaty is correctly matched?
x: Amherst concluded Yandabo (1826); Salbai was Warren Hastings', Amritsar 1809 Minto I's and Lahore Hardinge I's.

s: Which Act created the office of Governor-General of Bengal?
x: The Regulating Act of 1773 created the office of Governor-General of Bengal, with Warren Hastings as its first holder.

s: Who became the first Governor-General of India under the Charter Act of 1833?
x: Bentinck became the first Governor-General of India under the Charter Act of 1833; Canning was the first Viceroy.

s: Which one of the following correctly represents the successive changes in the title of the head of British administration in India?
o: Governor of Bengal → Governor-General of Bengal → Governor-General of India → Viceroy
Governor-General of Bengal → Governor of Bengal → Viceroy → Governor-General of India
Governor of Bengal → Governor-General of India → Governor-General of Bengal → Viceroy
Governor of Bengal → Viceroy → Governor-General of Bengal → Governor-General of India
x: The sequence was Governor of Bengal, Governor-General of Bengal from 1773, Governor-General of India from 1833, and Viceroy from 1858.

s: Who was the first Governor of Bengal (1758)?
x: Robert Clive became the first Governor of Bengal in 1758; Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal (1773).

s: Which Act created the office of Viceroy and Governor-General?
x: The Government of India Act, 1858 created the title Viceroy, first held by Lord Canning; the Charter Act of 1833 created the Governor-General of India.

s: Which Governor-General followed Cornwallis's second term in 1805?
x: Cornwallis's second term (1805) was followed by Sir George Barlow and then by Minto I; Wellesley served before it.

s: During whose tenure was the Charter Act of 1813 passed?
x: The Charter Act of 1813 was passed at the transition between Minto I and Marquess Hastings, whose tenure began in 1813.

s: Which Governor-General immediately preceded Marquess Hastings (1813-23)?
x: Minto I served 1807-13 and was followed by Marquess Hastings; the Charter Act of 1813 fell in this change-over.

s: Who served as Governor-General between William Bentinck and Auckland?
x: Sir Charles Metcalfe (1835-36) came between Bentinck (1828-35) and Auckland (1836-42).

s:
Arrange the following Governors-General in chronological order:
1. Amherst
2. Minto I
3. Auckland
4. Wellesley
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Wellesley (1798–1805), Minto I (1807–13), Amherst (1823–28) and Auckland (1836–42).

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Wellesley established the College of Fort William in 1800. The Anti-Slavery Act was associated with Ellenborough, while the Permanent Settlement and Cornwallis Code belonged to Cornwallis.

s: Who concluded the Treaty of Amritsar (1809) with Ranjit Singh?
x: Minto I concluded the Treaty of Amritsar in 1809; Bentinck's treaty of perpetual friendship with Ranjit Singh came in 1831.

s: Under which Governor-General was the Mahalwari system (1822), associated with Holt Mackenzie, introduced?
x: Mahalwari was introduced in 1822 under Marquess Hastings; Bentinck later revised it by Regulation IX of 1833.

s: Who introduced the Subsidiary Alliance (1798)?
x: Wellesley introduced the Subsidiary Alliance in 1798.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: The Treaty of Lahore of 1846 was concluded during Hardinge I's tenure, not Ellenborough's. Dalhousie set up the Public Works Department, Auckland started famine relief, and Hardinge I was associated with the Anti-Human-Sacrifice Act.

s: Who founded the College of Fort William (1800)?
x: The College of Fort William (1800) was Wellesley's, not Warren Hastings'.

s: In which year did the Vellore Mutiny break out during the tenure of Sir George Barlow?
x: The Vellore Mutiny took place in 1806, when Sir George Barlow was Governor-General.

s: With whom is the policy of non-intervention associated?
x: Sir John Shore followed non-intervention; Marquess Hastings followed a policy of intervention and wars.

s: Which Governor-General extended irrigation and started famine relief?
x: Auckland extended irrigation and started famine relief; Ellenborough ended the Afghan War.

s: To whose tenure do the Anglo-Nepal War (1814-16) and the Treaty of Sugauli belong?
x: Marquess Hastings fought the Anglo-Nepal War (1814-16), ended by the Treaty of Sugauli.

s: Under which Governor-General did the First Anglo-Burmese War (1824) take place?
x: Amherst fought the First Anglo-Burmese War (1824), ended by the Treaty of Yandabo (1826); the Second Burmese War was under Dalhousie.

s: During whose tenure did the First Anglo-Afghan War (1838) begin?
x: The First Anglo-Afghan War began in 1838 under Auckland; Ellenborough later ended the Afghan War.

s: During whose tenure was the Treaty of Lahore (1846) signed?
x: The Treaty of Lahore (1846), after the First Anglo-Sikh War, belongs to Hardinge I, not Ellenborough.

s: What was the real name of Marquess Hastings?
x: Marquess Hastings was Francis Rawdon-Hastings, also called Lord Moira.

s: Who is called the 'heaven-born general' and the founder of British power in India?
x: Robert Clive is called the founder of British power in India and the 'heaven-born general'.

s: Under which Governor-General was the Anti-Slavery Act of 1843 passed?
x: The 1843 Anti-Slavery Act was Ellenborough's; Hardinge I is linked to the Anti-Human-Sacrifice Act of 1845.

s: Under whom was the press in India liberated?
x: Metcalfe liberated the press; Bentinck suppressed Thuggee, Dalhousie set up the PWD and Hastings had the Code of Gentoo Laws compiled.

s: Under which Governor-General was the Anti-Human-Sacrifice Act of 1845 passed?
x: The Anti-Human-Sacrifice Act came in 1845 under Hardinge I; Ellenborough is linked with the abolition of slavery (1843).

s:
Consider the following statements about Dalhousie:
1. He applied the Doctrine of Lapse.
2. He ended the Afghan War.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Dalhousie is linked with the Doctrine of Lapse; the Afghan War was ended by Ellenborough.

s: Which Governor-General showed a preference for English education?
x: Hardinge I is noted for his preference for English education.

s: In which year did the Ceded Districts come to the Company under Wellesley?
x: The Nizam's alliance came in 1798, the Ceded Districts in 1800, and Andhra was merged into Madras in 1801.

s: Who described himself as the 'Bengal Tiger'?
x: Richard Colley Wellesley called himself the 'Bengal Tiger'; Clive was the 'heaven-born general'.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Hardinge I – Caste Disabilities Removal Act
x: The Caste Disabilities Removal Act (1850) was passed under Dalhousie, not Hardinge I.

s: Under whom was the Widow Remarriage Act passed in 1856?
x: The Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act was passed in July 1856 under Canning, who took over from Dalhousie in February 1856; it had been drafted during Dalhousie's tenure.
